newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds seen consolidating after late fall.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds seen consolidating after late fall.

text.p: German Bunds sank in late Thursday dealings to their lowest levels this week, after U.S. Treasuries dipped following U.S jobless claims data. But dealers said the upward trend was still intact.
Traders said the afternoon's losses were not that serious, but said how the U.S. market digests the unemployment numbers overnight would be crucial for Bunds on Friday.

The March Bund future contract was down 62 basis points to a day's low of 100.83 by 1600 GMT, while the benchmark 10-year Bund was down at 103.57, yielding 5.74 percent, up from 5.63 percent earlier in the day.
The U.S. Labor department said jobless claims fell 8,000 to 336,000 in the week ended November 30 from an upwardly revised 344,000 the prior week, just under the 337,000 average forecast.

In the morning Bunds had reached their session high when German November unemployment data came in higher-than-expected, dampening inflation worries. November unemployment rose 50,000 to 4.1 million on a seasonally adjusted basis.
But later the market was discouraged when the Bundesbank left key interest rates unchanged, although the decision had been largely expected.
"The (German) unemployment figures pulled the market up, but the unchanged rates disappointed," said one dealer.
But dealers said hopes that the German central bank would cut interest rates in the coming months would continue TO support the market.
"The market needs time to reflect at little," said Ian Ford, analyst at MCM YieldWatch. "We should tread water until the year-end but then firm up again if rate cut speculation haeats up."
Dealers noted that the LIFFE expiry of the December Bund future at midday had put some pressure on the March future.
